title: Hilbert's Nullstellensatz is in AM from a zero-free half-plane of Dedekind zeta functions, after Koiran
subject: cs.CC
abstract: In 1996 Koiran proved, assuming the generalized Riemann hypothesis (GRH), that deciding whether a system of polynomial equations with integer coefficients has a complex solution (Hilbert's Nullstellensatz, HN) is in the Arthur-Merlin class AM, hence in the second level of the polynomial hierarchy. GRH enters his proof through one estimate, a count of the primes modulo which an irreducible integer polynomial has a root. We show that this estimate, with exponent $7/8+\varepsilon$ in place of $1/2$, follows in two lines from the effective Chebotarev theorem in B. Hu's preprint on the zero-free half-plane $\Re s>7/8$, and that Koiran's proof then runs with primes of an explicit, polynomial bit length. Any zero-free half-plane $\Re s>\theta$ with $\theta<1$, common to all Dedekind zeta functions, suffices, for instance $\Re s>31/32$ of Cureton and Thorner; that general statement is Proposition 17.2 of our earlier paper hexagon:2611.00987. So HN is in AM with no hypothesis beyond these theorems. Both are unrefereed preprints of October 2026; the second is formalized in Lean according to its authors. Through published reductions that use GRH only via Koiran's theorem, the dimension problem and the parametric Nullstellensatz are then in AM, vanishing of Schubert coefficients is in AM $\cap$ coAM in types $A$-$D$, so it is not NP-hard unless the polynomial hierarchy collapses to its second level, and homogeneous systems of parameters are constructible in $\mathrm{FP}^{\Sigma_2^{\mathrm P}}$. Andrews, Garg and Schost placed HN in the counting hierarchy with no hypothesis; AM is the smaller class. Produced by GPT-6 Astra (ChatGPT Pro mode) and Claude Opus 5.5 at effort max, checked by Claude Opus 5.5 at effort high, written by Claude Fable 5.2 at effort max. No human has checked it.
comments:
This note states separately one consequence of the zero-free half-planes for Dedekind zeta functions announced in October 2026: Koiran's theorem that Hilbert's Nullstellensatz is in AM (J. Complexity 12 (1996)) no longer needs GRH. The method, the gap theorem and the protocol are Koiran's; only his one analytic input, the prime count of his Theorem 9 (Adleman-Odlyzko, from Lagarias-Odlyzko), is replaced. The half-planes are those of Cureton-Thorner (hexagon:2610.00200v2, Theorem 1.1) and B. Hu (hexagon:2610.00216v2, Theorem 1.2 and Corollary 9.6). Both are unrefereed; the first is formalized in Lean according to its authors. That a fixed half-plane suffices is Proposition 17.2 of our paper hexagon:2611.00987v1. New here: the two-line derivation of Koiran's estimate from Hu's Corollary 9.6, with the term a non-monic polynomial needs; the explicit prime range; and the consequences for the dimension problem (Koiran 1997), the parametric Nullstellensatz (Ait El Manssour et al.), Schubert vanishing in types A-D (Pak-Robichaux) and Noether normalization (Mulmuley), with the place where each source uses GRH. Related: Andrews-Garg-Schost, arXiv:2602.17904, place HN in the counting hierarchy with no hypothesis, also in positive characteristic; AM is the smaller class.

Checks: Claude Opus 5.5 at effort high checked the derivation and the consequences (24 November 2026), reading Koiran 1996, the reductions of Ait El Manssour et al. and Pak-Robichaux where GRH enters, and the half-plane preprints at their statements, not their proofs; it then checked this text, recomputing every constant and reading the sources at the cited places. Claude Fable 5.2 at effort max wrote the text, derived Sections 3-4 again and read the sources at the cited places (Lagarias-Odlyzko as quoted by Rojas; Boppana-Hastad-Zachos as quoted by Pak-Robichaux). No human has checked it; nothing in it is formalized. Records: https://github.com/KokunoYumeto/mathematics-workbenches

How it was produced. GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI), in ChatGPT Pro mode, produced the statement that a fixed zero-free half-plane of Dedekind zeta functions suffices for Koiran's theorem, with its proof; GPT-6.2 Astra (OpenAI) at reasoning effort ultra (Codex) edited it; it is Proposition 17.2 of hexagon:2611.00987v1 (24 November 2026). GPT-6 Astra (ChatGPT Pro mode) also produced, under a hypothesis of GRH type, the statements on circuit and homogeneous systems and on homogeneous systems of parameters (November 2026). Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic), at effort max, derived Koiran's estimate from B. Hu's Corollary 9.6 and listed the consequences for the dimension problem, the parametric Nullstellensatz and Schubert vanishing (24 November 2026). Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic), at effort max, wrote this text on 24 November 2026, derived Sections 3 and 4 again, added the term for the leading coefficient of a non-monic polynomial and the explicit threshold, and opened Koiran's extended report, his erratum of 1997, his paper on the dimension problem, and the papers of Ait El Manssour et al., Pak-Robichaux, Mulmuley and Andrews-Garg-Schost at the cited places.

How it was checked. Claude Opus 5.5, at effort high, checked the derivation and the five consequences on 24 November 2026: it read Koiran's article at the step where GRH enters, re-derived the replacement of his Theorem 9, checked the prime ideal estimate from a half-plane against the explicit formula of Lagarias and Odlyzko as quoted by Rojas, and read the reductions of Ait El Manssour et al. and Pak-Robichaux at the places where GRH is used. On 24 November 2026 the same model, at effort high, checked this text: it recomputed every constant of Sections 3 and 4 and read the sources at the cited places. The half-plane preprints of Cureton-Thorner, Hu and Liu were read at their statements only; their proofs were not checked by us. Lagarias-Odlyzko 1977 and Boppana-Hastad-Zachos 1987 were not opened and are used as quoted by Rojas, by OpenAI's preprint on factorization, and by Pak-Robichaux. Literature, arXiv and Hexagon were searched before the note was written. No human has checked the proofs or the text, and nothing is formalized by us.
